summary: Residential parcel on Maryland Street north of Building 21, mostly 90 ft with a 65 ft north leg under the D4D, assigned to Phase 2C in the Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan. Under the 2017 DDA the lease of historic Building 21 is triggered within a year after completion of the building on E1.

milestones.text: Planning Commission certifies the Pier 70 Mixed-Use Project Final EIR (Case 2014-001272ENV, Motion 19976) and approves the Design for Development (Resolution 19980)

Port Commission approves the Disposition and Development Agreement with FC Pier 70, LLC (Resolution 17-43), consents to the Pier 70 Special Use District and the D4D (17-45) and the Development Agreement (17-47)
Mayor Lee signs the Development Agreement ordinance (Ordinance 224-17) and the rest of the project legislation after Board of Supervisors approval on October 31, 2017
Disposition and Development Agreement dated as of May 2, 2018; the Port approves the Phase 1 Submittal the same month
Groundbreaking for Phase 1 (horizontal infrastructure, Building 12, parks) announced by the Port
Phase 1 site preparation and demolition begin; utility and street construction on 20th, Maryland, Louisiana, 21st and 22nd Streets follows in March 2019
Final appraisal of Parcel E2 comes in below its DDA threshold value, triggering a Phase 1 'down market delay' that tolls the developer's deadlines to close on option parcels
Brookfield halts construction at the end of Phase 1 horizontal work, citing market conditions
City issues Notice of Completion for the Phase 1 infrastructure, described by Brookfield as a $150 million investment
Phase 1 streets and utilities accepted by the City and Port; streets around Pier 70 opened to the public in May 2024
Phase 1 down market delay reaches its 60-month maximum; the parties extend it by six months to December 26, 2026 while DDA amendments are drafted

Port Commission hears an informational report on proposed DDA amendments: parcel-specific outside dates, a Project-wide affordable rate of no less than 20% (327 stand-alone affordable units kept), 65-to-90 ft height increases on certain residential parcels, developer return cut from 18% to 14%, and a new phasing plan
Amendments to the DDA, Development Agreement and Master Lease expected before the Port Commission and Board of Supervisors 'by the end of this year or early next year'

open_questions: No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the August 11, 2026 informational report, which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved.

The SF YIMBY summary describing E-1A/E-1B as ~120,000 gsf of retail and arts space conflicts with the D4D's residential designation for E1; the underlying filing was not retrieved, so this is left as reported.
The geometry file notes E1's real footprint is irregular around Building 21; the D4D figure shows E1 as two pieces (a 90-ft block and a 65-ft north leg) either side of Building 21's setback.
